<p>“Ask me…”</p><p>Hye-na downed the drink in her glass before starting her questions.</p><p>“First question. Why is that man always in the Association President’s office?”</p><p>“That man?”</p><p>She was clearly talking about Nerus.</p><p>I had cast a perception-obscuring spell on him so that ordinary people wouldn’t see him, but it seemed Hye-na’s eyes could.</p><p>“Yeah, the guy who guided us when we entered the S-rank Gate. Why is he always sitting in the President’s office?”</p><p>I had planned to brush it off with some vague answer if she asked, but she was too precise for that.</p><p>“…”</p><p>As I silently stared at Hye-na, she refilled her glass and spoke.</p><p>“What? Did you talk to him too?”</p><p>“Huh? Talk?”</p><p>“Yeah, I ran into him once in the hallway and asked why he was there.”</p><p>“What did he say?”</p><p>“At first, he asked if I could see him, then seemed interested. Then he said he was here as a diplomat…”</p><p>“Hmm…”</p><p>“Right?”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>“That emperor from the Gate is in South Korea right now, isn’t he?”</p><p>“Hah… So you knew everything from the start?”</p><p>Hye-na had just been pretending not to know.</p><p>Han Ji-hyeok and I thought we had fooled everyone perfectly, but we were wrong.</p><p>There was no point hiding it anymore.</p><p>“Yeah, that’s right.”</p><p>“I knew it… Well, since I asked you my question, you ask me one too.”</p><p>“Me? I don’t have anything I’m curious about…”</p><p>We’d already spent training school together—we knew each other well enough by now.</p><p>“Then… since you told me your secret, I’ll tell you mine.”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>Hye-na exhaled a few times before revealing her secret.</p><p>“Don’t tell anyone, but… I’m actually a Psionic.”</p><p>“Wait, a Psionic? I thought you were just a brutally strong Awakened?”</p><p>“What did you say?”</p><p>“No, uh… that’s just shocking.”</p><p>If this was true, then Hye-na was an unregistered Psionic.</p><p>She was a Psionic hiding as a regular Awakened.</p><p>Psionics sometimes went berserk, so the Hunter Association classified concealing one’s Psionic status as a serious crime.</p><p>Unless you had an ability as unbelievable as Yu Hyeon-jeong’s—one that no one would believe even if you told them—there was no reason, nor any need, to take such a massive risk by hiding it.</p><p>“What kind of Ability is it?”</p><p>I was curious.</p><p>Kang Hye-na was a Hunter renowned for her physical prowess, so I couldn’t help but wonder—what kind of psychic Ability could someone with such overwhelming power have been hiding all this time?</p><p>“I can see things others can’t, and read things others can’t.”</p><p>“So that’s how you saw beings like Nerus, who normal people can’t perceive?”</p><p>“Yeah.”</p><p>“What do you mean by ‘read’?”</p><p>“···.”</p><p>Hye-na silently held out her glass. After we clinked and downed our drinks, she spoke.</p><p>“I can read the secrets people try to hide. It’s not like I can choose to read them whenever I want—sometimes it just happens against my will.”</p><p>“Hmm… that’s hard to wrap my head around.”</p><p>“Have you ever read me?”</p><p>“What?! What did you read?!”</p><p>I could feel a cold sweat trickling down my back.</p><p>Please, please, please—let the words out of Hye-na’s mouth *not* be the one secret I’ve been hiding more than anything else. I prayed silently. Again and again.</p><p>But as if to betray my desperate plea, Hye-na locked eyes with me and said,</p><p>“That you’re in *that* kind of relationship with your family?”</p><p>“···.”</p><p>“And that you’ve had relations with Min Se-rin, and with other women too. I’ve read it all. Don’t make that face. I didn’t *want* to read it—it just… ended up in my memory at some point.”</p><p>Thud.</p><p>I set my glass down and stood up from my chair.</p><p>What the hell was I supposed to say?</p><p>*Everything you saw was a lie.*</p><p>Should I go with the cliché—*Do you really think it’s possible to have that kind of relationship with your own family?*?</p><p>Or should I run to Echo right now and ask if there was any magic to erase or distort Hye-na’s memories?</p><p>Or… should I threaten her with force to keep her mouth shut about this for the rest of her life?</p><p>“Sit down.”</p><p>Just as my mind raced with possibilities, Hye-na spoke softly.</p><p>“I don’t think it’s weird. Really.”</p><p>“You expect me to believe that?”</p><p>Pretending I didn’t know would be pointless now.</p><p>If anything, her saying she *didn’t* find my depraved sex life strange was what unsettled me more.</p><p>“Listen. Do you think Awakened are the same as regular humans?”</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“I don’t. In fact, there are scholars who argue that Awakened and ordinary humans are entirely different species, based on research.”</p><p>“What are you getting at?”</p><p>“They may look similar and think and act like humans, but from the moment they Awakened, they became an entirely different species from humans… Don’t you get what I’m saying?”</p><p>“···.”</p><p>Hye-na gestured toward the chair, as if telling me to sit down.</p><p>Only after I took my seat did she continue speaking.</p><p>“That’s how I see it. Ever since I Awakened, I’ve never once thought of myself as human. It’s not that I think I’m superior to humans—it’s that I consider myself a completely different species.”</p><p>“Huuu…”</p><p>It was a question that had been debated ever since Awakened appeared.</p><p>Were Awakened truly the same species as humans? Or should they be classified as an entirely separate species?</p><p>And for good reason—research had revealed that their very genes were different from ordinary humans.</p><p>It had been confirmed that Awakened possessed genes so complex and chaotic that modern bioengineering couldn’t even begin to unravel them.</p><p>Was it a different species from humans? That was a moral, ethical, and social debate—but strictly from a scientific standpoint, Awakened *were* a different species from humans.</p><p>“So what’s your point?”</p><p>“I don’t think what Seong-hyeon did with his family counts as incest. Sure, it’s a little messy, but… the moment someone Awakens, they’re only family in a social sense. Biologically, there’s *zero* overlap. How can it be incest?”</p><p>I didn’t know whether to call this a relief or what.</p><p>My head was hot, my thoughts spinning.</p><p>“There! My secret’s out! Now it’s my turn to ask *you* something.”</p><p>“Haa… Fine, ask away.”</p><p>I’d given up on resisting a long time ago.</p><p>If anything, I was almost *grateful* that Hye-na classified Awakened as a separate species, meaning she didn’t see an Awakened having relations with their family as incest.</p><p>“My last question… Did you *really* not know I’ve liked you since the training academy days?”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>Silence fell.</p><p>Was she joking? Or serious?</p><p>“I knew you were dense, but I didn’t think it was *this* bad. You *seriously* had no idea? When I dragged *you*—the guy who refused to talk to anyone and always kept to himself—to train and eat with me every single day, you should’ve caught on by then, right? Everyone else in our cohort *did*…”</p><p>“Ah…”</p><p>Back in the academy, when I’d isolated myself from everyone, Hye-na had been the only one to reach out to me.</p><p>Even after I’d rejected her countless times, she’d kept coming back, and at some point, we’d become friends.</p><p>Our classmates would occasionally tease us as they passed by—“When are you two dating?”—but I’d just brushed it off as kids messing around.</p><p>Maybe it was because I was close with Hye-na, who had always been at the top of our class and the object of everyone’s admiration—maybe that’s why they were jealous.</p><p>Kang Hye-na was staring right at me.</p><p>“Yeah, I thought about it too… I was too young back then to realize, but looking back now, I think that’s how it was… So do you still like me?”</p><p>“I don’t know. That’s why I came here today—to figure out if I still like you or not.”</p><p>“How are you gonna figure it out?”</p><p>Hye-na stood up and started undressing.</p><p>“H-Hey! Stop! What the hell are you doing?!”</p><p>“I thought about pretending to be crazy and asking you for a kiss, but we’re not kids anymore. Asking for proof through a kiss would be weird, right? So… I think if we just sleep together, I’ll know for sure.”</p><p>“Stop! Hye-na! You’re drunk. This isn’t a joke.”</p><p>“I’m not joking.”</p><p>“Ugh…”</p><p>Hye-na finished undressing, stood up, and walked toward the bedroom. Then she turned around and asked,</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291627" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“You don’t want to?”</p><p>“…”</p><p>This was the first time I’d ever hesitated like this with a naked woman right in front of me.</p><p>And it wasn’t just because she was a friend.</p><p>“I-I don’t *not* want to… It’s just… You’ll definitely regret this. Put your clothes back on.”</p><p>“I won’t regret it. Why are *you* the one deciding that?”</p><p>“Last chance. You *really* won’t regret it?”</p><p>“Nope.”</p><p>I stood up from my chair, walked over to Hye-na, and grabbed her shoulders.</p><p>“Ah…”</p><p>“Fine. Then let’s start with a kiss. If we kiss and you don’t feel anything, we stop there. Deal?”</p><p>“Mm-hmm…”</p><p>Hye-na nodded deeply, her head bowed.</p><p>***</p><p>Chuup, chup, chuurrup—</p><p>“Nnngh—ah!”</p><p>“Hah… So? Still feel that fluttering? Still no regrets?”</p><p>“Shut up and open your mouth.”</p><p>“No, listen—mmpf!”</p><p>Chuurup—</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291628" loading="lazy">
</p><p>I *should* have told her to put her clothes back on right then and there.</p><p>Hye-na’s pounding heartbeat thrummed through my body.</p>
